mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate tighter credit conditions, which reduces the present value of future earnings and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in the next month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL of at least 2% over the next quarter is interpreted as persistent inflation pressure, which compresses real discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by at least 2% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day rolling average forward returns remain positive during the inflation episode (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of more than 50,000 jobs in a single month coincides with optimism about economic recovery, which elevates equity risk premia and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 50,000 in one month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the labor addition signal (out-of-sample t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) show simultaneous monthly increases above their prior month's levels, it signals expanding business and consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in >70% of such dual-positive months (rolling IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% predicts supply-side constraints that raise uncertainty and discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for three consecutive months by at least 3%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during the bottleneck (bootstrap p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 4.5% for two consecutive months is interpreted as a deepening labor market weakness, which lowers equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases for two consecutive months and remains above 4.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified weak-labor regime (median > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 10% in a given month, it signals strong consumer demand that supports optimism about corporate earnings and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by at least 10% relative to its 12-month moving average in the month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant during the identified surge (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of prolonged monetary easing (defined by FEDFUNDS < 1% for two consecutive months), the absence of a sharp rise in UNRATE, and with CPIAUCSL flat or declining, creates a risk-off environment that is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL flat or falling over the same period
regime_hint: prolonged low-rate environment without wage pressure
failure_condition: 20-day rolling average forward returns are positive during this regime (median > 0).
